To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Higgs bosons can mix with unparticle states, and that this can lead to an infrared divergence in the vacuum expectation value of the unparticle operator, which can be cured by introducing unparticle self-interaction.
the Higgs bosonic field mixes with the unparticle field and the unparticle field mixes with itself.

(i) a coupling between a Higgs boson and a scalar unparticles leads, after electrowek symmetry breaking, to an infrared divergent unparticle vacuum expectation value, (ii) such a vacuum expectation value can be made finite by introducing unparticle self-interaction, and (iii) the finite unparticle vacuum expectation can trigger the mixing between the Higgs bosons and the plasmon-like unparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phenomenology of a new class of models where a Higgs boson couples to a scalar unparticle.
the phenomenology of a Higgs-unparticle coupling, which is not only renormalizable but also UV finite.
the interplay between the Higgs sector and the sector of a new light scalar particle with a non-integer dimension, which is not protected by a gauge symmetry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a renormalizable coupling of the Higgs with a scalar unparticle field is phenomenologically viable.
the Higgs-unparticles interplay can be made phenomenologically viable and interesting.
the unparticle pole is a new and interesting feature of the Higgs sector, which is not a consequence of the Higgs mass, but rather a property of the Higgs potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a renormalizable Higgs-unparticle coupling, in the presence of a scale invariant unparticle self-coupling, triggers a Higgs-unparticle mixing which, in the unparticle sector, gives rise to a plasmon-like resonance with properties qualitatively distinct from those found in previous works.

a Higgs-unparticle mixing can trigger an unparticle excitation with properties reminiscent of the plasmon resonance, and that such excitation could be explored experimentually through the Higgs decay to unparticle pairs.
the Higgs-unparticles interplay could lead to a rich phenomenology, which could be explored in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs-unparticles coupling is renormalizable and can be made finite at the two-loop level.
the Higgs bosons could be a portal to unparticle physics.
the Higgs-unparticles interplay can lead to interesting new phenomenology, which is qualitatively different and richer than what is usually considered.
